# Pesticide Guide - Complete Knowledge Base
> Full data export and guide comparing official pesticide monitoring records (USDA PDP, EFSA, CFIA) and Food Compass 2.0 nutrition scores for 69 fruits, vegetables, and legumes across 9 international markets.

## Methodology Overview
- Total Lab Tests: 184,077 official government chemical monitoring samples.
- Pesticide Load Score (0-100): Relative score based on detection rate, multiple residue counts, and EPA chronic/acute benchmarks. Lower score means cleaner produce.
- Food Compass Score (0-100): Tufts University nutrient profiling system evaluating 54 nutrient attributes across 9 health domains. Higher score indicates richer nutrient density.
- Evidence Quality Index: High (>=80% coverage and >=100 samples), Moderate (>=60% coverage and >=40 samples), Limited (<40 samples).
- Washing Protocol: 1% baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) solution (1 tsp per 2 cups water) soaked for 12-15 minutes degrades 80-96% of surface residues, outperforming tap water.

## Produce Profiles Index (69 Foods)

### Apples (fruit)
- URL: https://pesticideguide.online/food/apples
- Pesticide Load Score: 66/100
- Food Compass 2.0 Score: 94/100 (exact match)
- Total Tested Samples: 7,174 tests (2014-2024)
- Benchmark Coverage: 85.8%
- Buying Recommendation: CONVENTIONAL WITH WASHING - Conventional is acceptable; wash with baking soda to lower residue.
- Reason: Moderate residue penetration. A 1% baking soda soak significantly reduces chemical exposure.
- Top Chemical Residues: Phosmet (detected in 1.5% of samples), Captan (sum of captan and THPI, expressed as captan) (detected in 15.2% of samples), Phosmet (detected in 1.5% of samples), Pyrimethanil (detected in 15.4% of samples)
